The net interest cost is calculated by applying the discount rate to the net balance of the defined benefit obligation
and the fair value of plan assets. This cost is included in employee benefit expense in the restated consolidated
statement of profit and loss.
Remeasurement gains and losses arising from experience adjustments and changes in actuarial assumptions are
recognised in the period in which they occur, directly in other comprehensive income. They are included in retained
earnings in the statement of changes in equity and in the Restated Consolidated Statement of Assets and Liabilities.
Changes in the present value of the defined benefit obligation resulting from plan amendments or curtailments are
recognised immediately in restated consolidated statement of profit and loss as past service cost.
Defined contribution plans
The Group pays provident fund contributions to publicly administered Provident Funds as per local regulations.
The Group has no further payment obligations once the contributions have been paid. The contributions are
accounted for as defined contribution plans and the contributions are recognised as employee benefit expense when
they are due.
Superannuation
Superannuation benefits for employees designated as chief managers and above are covered by Group policies
with the Life Insurance Corporation of India. Group’s contribution payable for the period/year is charged to
restated consolidated statement of profit and loss. There are no other obligations other than the annual contribution
payable.
National Pension Scheme (NPS)
In respect of employees who opt for contribution to the NPS, Group contribute a certain percentage of the total basic
salary of such employees to the aforesaid scheme, a defined contribution plan, which is managed and administered
by pension fund management companies. Such contributions are recognised in the restated consolidated statement of
profit and loss Account in the period/year in which they accrue.
Bonus plans
The Group recognises a liability and an expense for bonuses. The Group recognises a provision where
contractually obliged or where there is a past practice that has created a constructive obligation.
In case of the Parent Company and one of the subsidiary company, SEBI has laid down certain norms in terms of
the compensation policy for the key management personnel which are as under:
• The variable pay component will not exceed one third of the total pay.
• 50% of the variable pay will be paid on a deferred basis after three years.
(s) Contributed Equity shares are classified as equity
Incremental costs directly attributable to the issue of new shares are shown in equity as a deduction, net of tax,
from the proceeds.
(t) Dividends
Provision is made for the amount of any dividend declared, being appropriately authorised and no longer at the
discretion of the entity, on or before the end of the reporting period but not distributed at the end of the reporting
period.
(u) Earnings per share
Basic earnings per share
Basic earnings per share is calculated by dividing:
• the profit attributable to owners of the Group
• by the weighted average number of equity shares outstanding during the period/financial year, adjusted
for bonus elements in equity shares issued during the period/year.

Diluted earnings per share
Diluted earnings per share adjusts the figures used in the determination of basic earnings per share to take into
account:
• the after income tax effect of interest and other financing costs associated with dilutive potential equity
shares, and
• the weighted average number of additional equity shares that would have been outstanding assuming
the conversion of all dilutive potential equity shares.
(v) Non- Current assets held for Sale
Non-current assets (or disposal Groups) are classified as held for sale if their carrying amount will be recovered
principally through a sale transaction rather than through continuing use and a sale is considered highly probable.
They are measured at the lower of their carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell, except for assets such as
deferred tax assets, assets arising from employee benefits, financial assets and contractual rights under insurance
contracts, which are specifically exempt from this requirement.
An impairment loss is recognised for any initial or subsequent write-down of the asset (or disposal Group) to fair
value less costs to sell. A gain is recognised for any subsequent increases in fair value less costs to sell of an asset
(or disposal Group), but not in excess of any cumulative impairment loss previously recognised. A gain or loss not
previously recognised by the date of the sale of the non-current asset (or disposal Group) is recognised at the date
of de-recognition. Non-current assets (including those that are part of a disposal Group) are not depreciated or
amortised while they are classified as held for sale. Interest and other expenses attributable to the liabilities of a
disposal Group classified as held for sale continue to be recognised.
Non-current assets classified as held for sale and the assets of a disposal group classified as held for sale are
presented separately from the other assets in the Restated Consolidated Statement of Assets and Liabilities. The
liabilities of a disposal group classified as held for sale are presented separately from other liabilitiesin the Restated
Consolidated Statement of Assets and Liabilities.
A discontinued operation is a component of the entity that has been disposed of or is classified as held for sale and
that represents a separate major line of business or geographical area of operations, is part of a single co-ordinated
plan to dispose of such a line of business or area of operations, or is a subsidiary acquired exclusively with a view
to resale. The results of discontinued operations are presented separately in the restated consolidated statement of
profit and loss.

The goodwill is tested for impairment at least annually or more frequently if events or changes in circumstances indicate that it might be impaired. For impairment testing, goodwill arising
on acquisition of business, is allocated to a cash generating unit “CGU” representing the lowest level of group of assets that generates independent cash flows within the Group at which
goodwill is monitored for internal management reporting purposes.
The recoverable amount of the CGU is determined as higher of fair value less cost to sell and value in use. The Group determine the value in use of the CGU using the income approach,
based on future cash flows, after considering current economic conditions and trends, estimated future operating results, growth rates and anticipated future economic conditions. The Group
assesses the valuation methodology based upon the relevance and availability of the data at the time the valuation is performed.
The Group had evaluated goodwill for impairment as at the end of the reporting period i.e., March 31, 2026, March 31, 2025 and March 31, 2024 based on the future cash flows and other
factors of the related CGUs. Basis the said evaluation performed by the Group, the carrying amount does not exceed the recoverable amount of the cash generating units. Accordingly, there
was no impairment recorded for the year ended March 31, 2026, March 31, 2025 and March 31, 2024. Subsequent to year ended March 31, 2026 and March 31, 2025, there were no
identifiable events or indications for impairment. Accordingly, there was no impairment recognised for the three months periods ended June 30, 2026 and June 30, 2025.
Further, the Management believes that any reasonably possible change in the key assumptions would not cause the carrying amount to exceed the recoverable amount of the cash generating
units.

Particulars
NSE has only one class of equity shares having a par value of ₹1 per share. They entitle the holder to participate in dividends. In the event of liquidation of NSE, the holders of equity shares
will be entitled to receive remaining assets of NSE, after distribution of all preferential amounts. The distribution will be in proportion to the number of equity shares held by the shareholders.
Every holder of equity shares present at a meeting in person or by proxy is entitled to one vote and upon a poll each share is entitled to one vote.

Vidyamandir/284) dated March 20, 2019 in relation to aforesaid matter. NSE has given effect to this judgment with effect from April 1, 2019. In NSE's assessment, this did not have a significant

NSE had received three separate Show Cause Notices (SCN) from Securities and Exchange
Board of India (“SEBI”) on May 22, 2017, July 03, 2018, and July 31, 2018, against NSE
and some of its former employees, in respect of NSE’s Colocation facility (“Colocation”),
Dark Fibre (“Dark Fibre”) and Governance and conflict of interest related matters
(“Governance and COI”). Subsequently, SEBI’s Whole-Time Member ("WTM") passed
orders in respect of all the three SCNs vide its letter dated April 30, 2019.
SEBI WTM vide its order dated April 30, 2019 directed NSE inter-alia to disgorge an
amount of ₹6,248.90 million along with interest at the rate of 12% per annum from April
01, 2014, till the actual date of payment and certain non-monetary and restrictive directions
including prohibiting NSE from accessing securities market, for a period of six months
from the date of the order (“Colocation WTM Order”). SEBI Adjudicating Officer ("AO")
had also passed an order dated February 10, 2021 (“Colocation AO Order”) covering the
above issues pertaining to Colocation and levied a monetary penalty of ₹10 million on
NSE. NSE preferred appeals before the Hon’ble Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT)
against the Colocation WTM Order and the Colocation AO Order.

issues pertaining to Governance and conflict of interest and levied a monetary penalty of
₹10 million on NSE. NSE filed separate appeals before the SAT against the Governance

The Group’s business activities expose it to a variety of financial risks, namely liquidity risk, market risks and credit risk. The Group's risk management policies are established to
identify and analyse the risks faced by the Group, to set appropriate risk limits and controls and to monitor risks and adherence to limits. Risk management policies and systems are
reviewed regularly to reflect changes in market conditions and the Group's activities. The Group's senior management has the overall responsibility for developing and implementing
the Group's risk management policies. The Group has constituted a Risk Management Committee to oversee the implementation of the Group's risk management policies.
The Risk Management Committee of the Group is supported by the Treasury Committee that provides assurance that the Group's financial risk activities are governed by appropriate
policies and procedures and that financial risks are identified, measured and managed in accordance with the Group's policies and risk objectives.
There is a dedicated Treasury department to ensure Treasury investments are made as per the approved Prudential norms of Investment.
Liquidity risk is the risk that the Group will face difficulties in meeting its obligations associated with its financial liabilities. The Group’s approach to managing liquidity is to ensure
that it will have sufficient funds to meet its liabilities when due without incurring avoidable costs. In doing this, management considers both normal and stressed conditions. A material
and sustained shortfall in Group's cash flow could impair investor confidence.
The Group maintained a cautious funding strategy, with a positive cash balance throughout the three months periods ended June 30, 2026 and June 30, 2025 and years ended March
31, 2026; March 31, 2025 and March 31, 2024. Cash flows from operating and investing activities provides the funds to service the financing of liabilities on a day-to-day basis.
The Group's treasury department regularly monitors the rolling forecasts to ensure it has sufficient cash on an on-going basis to meet operational needs. Any short term surplus cash
generated by the operations, over and above the amount required for working capital management and other operational requirements, is retained as cash and cash equivalents (to the
extent required) and any excess is invested in interest bearing deposits and other marketable debt investments not invested in equity linked funds including the government securities,
mutual funds and exchange traded funds with appropriate maturities to optimise the cash returns on investments while ensuring sufficient liquidity to meet its liabilities.

Particulars
Treasury team of Finance department performs the valuations of financial assets for financial reporting purposes. This team reports to the Chief Financial Officer (CFO). Valuation for various levels of financial instruments are derived as per the below process.
Level 1 : The Valuation is based on quoted prices in active markets, for the financial assets. This is the most reliable input and is given the highest priority. This Includes debt mutual funds, whose NAV are derived from the authentic sources and quoted equity instruments listed on Stock exchange.
Level 2 : Inputs other than quoted prices in active markets that are observable, either directly or indirectly. This includes Government securities whose valuation are conducted based on observable data like interest rates or yield curves.
Level 3 : This Valuation in based on inputs that are not based on observable market data and may require an entity to make assumptions or judgments about future cash flows or other factors. This includes Unquoted Equity Instrument.
At the period/year-end external valuers are engaged to provide independent valuation of level 3 instruments.
The valuation of financial assets as per the above process is conducted at every reporting period, by the Treasury team and discussed with CFO.

which there were no material foreseeable losses. The Group did not have any derivative contracts outstanding as at June 30, 2026; June 30, 2025; March 31, 2026; March 31, 2025 and March 31, 2024.
The Board of Directors of NSE Investments Limited (NIL), in its meeting held on February 1, 2023 had granted an in-principle approval for the sale / divestment of Education and Technology
Businesses. Pending required regulatory approval, the management had classified the business operations of Education Business and Technology Business as discontinued operations as they meet the
conditions as prescribed under Ind AS 105 - Non-current Assets Held for Sale and Discontinued Operations from the year ended 31 March 2023. Details of discontinued operations, Assets held for sale
and liabilities directly associated with assets classified as held for sale is given below. Education Business is held through NAL Academy Limited (NAL) (Formerly known as NSE Academy Limited),
Talentsprint Private Limited and TalentSprint Inc. and Technology Business is held through NSEIT Limited, NSEIT (US) Inc., Aujas Cybersecurity Limited and Nusummit Technologies Private Limited
(formerly known as CXIO Technologies Private Limited).
NSEIT Limited, a subsidiary company of NIL, transferred its Technology Business (excluding Digital Examination Business) on a slump sale basis along with three of its other wholly owned subsidiaries
during the year ended March 31, 2025. Further, during the year ended March 31, 2025, NIL has also disposed of its entire equity stake in NSEIT. The above transactions resulted in a gain of ₹6,540.28
million (net of tax), which has been recognised in the Restated Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss for the year ended March 31, 2025.
On April 22, 2025, NAL a wholly owned subsidiary of the Group, has divested its entire equity stake in TalentSprint Private Limited along with its wholly owned subsidiary, TalentSprint Inc for a total
consideration of ₹2,448.54 million (subject to working capital adjustments). The above transactions including true up by ₹1.5 million, resulted in a gain of ₹1,141.39 million (net of tax), which has been
recognised during the three months period ended June 30, 2025 and year ended March 31, 2026.
The subsidiary company, NAL post approval from its Board of Directors and its shareholders, applied to National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) to initiate process of capital reduction, of up to
2,41,32,00,000 Preference Shares of ₹10 each for an aggregate consideration of up to and not exceeding ₹2,413.20 million, under the provisions of Section 66 and other applicable provisions of the
Companies Act, 2013 (“Act”) and in terms of the National Company Law Tribunal (Procedure for Reduction of Share Capital of Company) Rules 2016. The said application was made to NCLT on
14th July 2025 and the final order has been received from NCLT on June 17, 2026.
The Board of Directors of NAL at its meeting held on June 29, 2026, approved the implementation of the NCLT Order and authorised the filing of Form INC-28 with the Registrar of Companies
("ROC"). Accordingly, NAL filed Form INC-28 with the ROC on July 9, 2026. NAL is taking steps to implement the order and complete the process of capital reduction by September 30, 2026.
The Investment Committee of NIL in its meeting held on July 4, 2025, had approved the sale of KRA business owned by NSE Data & Analytics Limited (NDAL) by way of Business Transfer
Agreement (BTA) to Computer Age Management Services Limited (CAMS) for a total consideration of ₹70.00 million. NDAL and CAMS executed a definitive agreement on July 31, 2025. NDAL has
received SEBI NOC vide the letter dated October 1, 2025 to sell the KRA business. NDAL has transferred the KRA Business on January 5, 2026 to CAMS. The above transaction resulted in a gain of
₹49.68 million (net of tax), which has been recognised during the year ended March 31, 2026.
The management has classified the business operations of Education Business under NAL, KRA Business of NDAL as discontinued operations as per Ind AS 105 - Non-current Assets Held for Sale and
Discontinued Operations. The Consolidated Restated Financial Information for the comparative years ended March 31, 2025 and 2024 also included technology business.
The Board of Directors of NSE Investments Limited in its meeting held on October 10, 2024, noted that the proposed merger of NSE Data & Analytics Limited and NSE Indices Limited is on hold as
NSE Indices Limited is proposed to be regulated as Index Provider under SEBI (Index Provider) Regulations, 2024 and NSE Data & Analytics operates NSE KRA business which is a SEBI regulated
intermediary.

Overview
We have been the largest stock exchange in India in terms of total turnover in cash market and total turnover in equity 
derivatives (based on notional turnover for equity options) from Fiscal 20011 to Fiscal 2026 and the three months period ended 
June 30, 2026, and have also been the largest stock exchange in India in terms of total turnover in exchange-traded currency 
derivatives (based on notional turnover for currency options) from Fiscal 20092 to Fiscal 2026 and three months period ended 
June 30, 2026, according to the Redseer Report. According to World Federation of Exchanges, compared to the leading listed 
stock exchange groups globally, we were the largest multi-asset class exchange in terms of number of trades in cash equities 
and contracts traded in equity derivatives in Fiscal 2026 and the three months period ended June 30, 2026, with a global market 
share of 11.38% in number of trades in cash equities and 51.18% in contracts traded in equity derivatives in Fiscal 2026, and a 
global market share of 10.68% in number of trades in cash equities and 50.22% in contracts traded in equity derivatives in the 
three months period ended June 30, 2026. We are a “first level regulator” in India3
, and in that role are committed to providing 
equal, unrestricted, transparent and fair access to the stock market to all market participants, including investors, issuers and 
intermediaries, while maintaining orderly and efficient market functioning and safeguarding investor interests. 
We operate a vertically integrated stock exchange - where we offer a simple, integrated platform for trading, clearing, listing 
and other services such as data feed services, data terminal services and licensing services. We provide a comprehensive, one￾stop platform to manage regulatory compliance, risk monitoring, and post-trade settlement. We offer a diversified range of 
products across multiple asset classes, including cash market, futures, options, mutual funds platform, commodity derivatives, 
exchange-traded currency derivatives, wholesale debt market and interest rate futures, among others. Our operations are 
supported by our proprietary technology infrastructure that is resilient and secure, supporting high-speed and high-frequency 
transactions while ensuring seamless market operations, comprehensive market data dissemination, and allows for rapid 
implementation of regulatory directives.

Regulatory Oversight and Governmental Policies
We operate in a highly regulated industry and are subject to extensive regulation. We are a “first level regulator” in India, and 
in that role are committed to providing equal, unrestricted, transparent and fair access to the stock market to all market 
participants, including investors, issuers and intermediaries, while maintaining orderly and efficient market functioning and 
safeguarding investor interests. SEBI regulates us and has broad powers to approve or consent to proposals made by us, whether 
with respect to rule amendments, product range or infrastructure or market development initiatives. SEBI may also conduct 
periodic reviews, audits and inspections and issue suspension orders of our stock exchange. While regulation can constrain 
certain activities, it also reinforces market integrity and investor confidence, which are foundational to sustained volume 
growth. Below are some examples of key recent regulations introduced by SEBI and RBI that impacted our results of 
operations: 
• In January 2024, RBI issued revised directions governing exchange traded currency derivatives traded on stock 
401
exchanges and clearing corporations. Under the updated framework, these entities shall not deal in or otherwise 
undertake the business relating to foreign exchange derivatives unless they hold an authorisation issued by the RBI. 
Stock exchanges are permitted to offer foreign exchange derivative contracts in specified currency pairs to both 
resident and non-resident participants, with the RBI mandating that exchange-traded rupee derivatives be used only 
for hedging purposes, alongside documentation and position limit requirements designed to ensure activity reflects 
genuine exposure. In addition, where a participant’s open position exceeds US$100 million, the relevant stock 
exchange must report day-end and intra-day peak position data to the designated authorised dealer or custodian. These 
changes were one of the reasons for a decline in currency derivatives volumes.
• SEBI introduced a series of measures during Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2026 to strengthen the equity index derivatives 
framework, implemented in phases. Among the most structurally significant were the rationalisation of weekly 
expiries for index options, restricting each exchange to a single weekly expiry for one benchmark index effective 
November 2024, and the standardisation of expiry days across exchanges, with our contracts moving to Tuesday 
expiry effective September 2025. Additional measures included increasing the minimum contract size for index 
derivatives, imposing additional margin requirements on short options contracts on expiry days, mandating upfront 
collection of option premiums, tighter position limit monitoring, refined methodologies for measuring open interest 
and effective exposures, enhanced intraday surveillance mechanisms and recalibration of risk management and margin 
frameworks for index derivatives. These measures increased margin discipline, reduced the scope for concentrated or 
leveraged short-term positioning, and aligned derivatives activity more closely with underlying cash market liquidity, 
according to the Redseer Report. While intended to curb excessive speculation and protect retail investors, these 
measures have moderated speculative turnover and contributed to a decline in trading volumes in equity futures and 
equity options and related revenue in Fiscal 2026. 
• Pursuant to SEBI’s circular dated October 1, 2024, clearing corporations with a clearing volume share of 40% or more 
are required to maintain a minimum Core Settlement Guarantee Fund (“Core SGF”) corpus of ₹105,000 million for 
equity derivatives products. This requirement reflects the introduction of additional stress testing scenarios for 
determining the minimum Core SGF corpus. On March 23, 2023, the Governing Board approved a voluntary 
contribution of 2% of transaction charges to the Core SGF. Accordingly, NSE Clearing Limited (“NCL”) augmented 
the Core SGF corpus to the prescribed minimum of ₹105,000 million for equity derivatives products, achieving 
compliance by December 31, 2024. Subsequently, in February 2025, our Governing Board approved the 
discontinuation of our voluntary contribution of 2% of transaction charges to the Core SGF with effect from January 
1, 2025, following the Core SGF having been adequately funded. Accordingly, during Fiscal 2026, we contributed 
₹5.76 million to the Core SGF, as against ₹2,340.89 million contributed in the preceding Fiscal 2025. During the three 
months period ended June 30, 2026, a further contribution of ₹50.00 million by NSE and ₹50.00 million by NCL was 
made to the Core SGF towards new products added in electronic gold receipts. Additionally, ₹2,500.00 million 
earmarked from General Reserves for the Commodity Derivatives SGF in Fiscal 2019 was de-allocated and reinstated 
during Fiscal 2024, pursuant to SEBI’s approval dated January 31, 2024.
• SEBI issued its “True to Label” circular on July 1, 2024, requiring stock exchanges and other market infrastructure 
institutions to adopt a uniform charge structure for all members. Previously, members could collect charges from end 
clients at higher rates while paying the exchange at lower aggregate rates. This circular eliminated this practice by 
requiring that charges recovered from clients correspond to those received by the stock exchanges. While this required 
us to redesign our transaction charge structures, the revised pricing closely replicated our existing average realisation 
rates and did not have a material impact on our revenue.
• Pursuant to the Union Budget for Fiscal 2027, Securities Transaction Tax (STT) rates applicable to equity derivatives 
were revised with effect from April 1, 2026. STT on equity futures increased from 0.02% to 0.05% of the contract 
value, STT on equity options premium was increased from 0.10% to 0.15%, and STT on option exercise was increased 
from 0.125% to 0.15%. These revisions were introduced with the stated objective of curbing excessive speculative 
trading in the futures and options products, and the higher transaction cost structure may affect participation levels, 
particularly in high-frequency or leveraged strategies, and could moderate derivatives turnover and liquidity depth, 
while STT on delivery-based equity transactions remains unchanged. Our Company’s contribution to exchequer 
(including collections and payments) is ₹ 593.27 billion in Fiscal 2026, of which STT/Commodity Transaction Tax 
(CTT) is ₹ 483.47 billion, income tax is ₹ 46.18 billion, stamp duty is ₹ 34.11 billion, GST is ₹ 19.43 billion and fees 
paid to SEBI is ₹ 10.08 billion. Of the total STT/CTT of ₹ 483.47 billion, cash market (delivery based) segment 
constituted 46.82%, cash market (intraday) segment constituted 7.20%, and equity derivatives segment constituted 
45.98%. Our Company’s contribution to exchequer (including collections and payments) is ₹205.76 billion in the 
three months period ended June 30, 2026, of which STT/Commodity Transaction Tax (CTT) is ₹183.13 billion, 
income tax is ₹3.73 billion, stamp duty is ₹9.80 billion, GST is ₹6.57 billion and fees paid to SEBI is ₹ 2.54 billion, 
respectively. Of the total STT/CTT of ₹183.13 billion, cash market (delivery based) segment constituted 36.73%, cash 
market (intraday) segment constituted 6.35%, and equity derivatives segment constituted 56.92% in the three months 
period ended June 30, 2026.
• Pursuant to SEBI’s Circular dated January 16, 2026, closing auction session (“CAS”) has been introduced in the equity 
cash segment of stock exchanges and revised the pre-open auction session framework. Initially, CAS will apply only 
to stocks in the cash segment for which derivative contracts are available and the closing price for other securities 
continues to be determined based on volume weighted average price of trades executed during the last 30 minutes of 
402
the continuous trading session. The framework for CAS has become effective from August 3, 2026 and the framework 
for pre-open auction session revised the duration of certain sessions within the pre-open auction window which will 
become effective from September 7, 2026.
• Pursuant to the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Credit Facilities) Amendment Directions, 2026 (Revised) 
dated March 30, 2026 (“Directions”), a new chapter, Chapter XIII A – Credit Facilities to Capital Market 
Intermediaries (“CMI”) has been inserted, applicable to lending to CMIs, as defined under the Directions. The 
Directions enables banks to extend need-based credit facilities to CMIs for day-to-day operations, including margin 
trading and settlement-related timing mismatches, issue guarantees on behalf of brokers/clearing members in favour 
of exchanges or clearing houses, and custodian banks may issue irrevocable payment commitments, in favour of a 
clearing corporation of a stock exchange. Barring specified exceptions, all credit facilities to CMIs, including intraday 
facilities, must be fully secured (100 per cent collateral). These amendments come into force from July 1, 2026, or an 
earlier date when adopted by a bank in entirety.
Changes in policies by GoI or foreign governments may relate to, among others, monetary or tax law or policy, tax treaties,

Interest rates and funds available for investment
We earn income from investment and treasury activities. The funds available for investment are primarily derived from two 
principal pools: (a) margin funds, comprising cash collaterals from clearing members and deposits received from trading 
members; and (b) our own surplus funds. These funds are invested primarily in government securities, fixed deposits, mutual 
funds (including overnight and liquid schemes of the highest credit quality) and corporate bonds, in accordance with our 
investment policy and applicable SEBI prudential norms. On our balance sheet, the investments attributable to each of these 
pools are reported under “Investments” (both non-current and current), other financial assets (non-current), cash and cash 
equivalents, and “bank balances other than cash and cash equivalents”. The income earned on such investments depends 
principally on (i) prevailing interest rates and market rates of return, and (ii) the quantum of funds available for investment 
across each of the two pools described above, which are in turn influenced by the macroeconomic environment in India and 
levels of market activity. The key characteristics of each pool are as follows:
- Margin fund- NCL and NSEICC requires its clearing members to deposit collateral for margin trading and settlement of 
trades. These deposits are held by NCL and NSEICC at banks primarily as fixed deposits that can be redeemed at short 
notice. Under Ind AS, since the deposits are made with NCL and NSEICC, they appear on our Restated Consolidated 
Statement of Assets and Liabilities as bank balances on the asset side, with a corresponding liability entry. The quantum 
of cash collateral available for investment is determined by the margin policy applicable to the relevant trade, prevailing 
levels of market activity and open interest, and the applicable settlement period. As trading volumes and open interest 
increase, the pool of margin funds available for investment correspondingly expands, and vice versa. As of June 30, 2026 
₹260,124.27 million, pertained to settlement obligations and margin money from members, compared to ₹301,466.62 
million as of March 31, 2026, ₹158,798.86 million as of March 31, 2025 and ₹213,271.10 million as of March 31, 2024.
- Own surplus funds- Our profitability is underpinned by consistent and sustained cash generation, and we had no 
outstanding loans or borrowings as of June 30, 2026. However, certain bank guarantees have been availed for our clearing 
operations. We have an active treasury management function that invests our own surplus funds, generating investment 
income which is classified as other income. This pool is influenced by our retained earnings, dividend distribution policy 
and capital allocation decisions. We maintain a risk reserve by earmarking certain of our treasury investments on our 
balance sheet, as determined by our Governing Board on an annual basis. This reserve is earmarked on a voluntary basis, 
out of retained earnings, as a buffer against potential losses arising from risks inherent in our business activities, including 
operational risk, member default risk and other extreme but plausible scenarios of exposures inherent to the Exchange's 
activities. We assessed reserve requirement towards adequate risk capital management and transferred an excess amount 
of ₹37,280.00 million for the Fiscal 2026, from risk reserves to retained earnings within equity leading to a decrease in the
risk reserve to ₹48,050.00 million as of March 31, 2026 from ₹85,330.00 million as of March 31, 2025. As of June 30, 
2026 and June 30, 2025, the risk reserve was ₹48,050.00 million and ₹85,330.00 million, respectively. As of June 30, 
2026, the investments earmarked towards the risk reserve amounted to ₹28,704.00 million within non-current investments, 
and ₹19,346.00 million within current investments. The reduction in risk reserves from June 30, 2025 to June 30, 2026, 
and from March 31, 2025 to March 31, 2026, primarily reflected revised assessmentsrelating to member defaults, including 
enhanced safeguards such as the pledge/re-pledge framework and upstreaming of cash collateral, periodic assessment of 
the adequacy of the Investor Protection Fund Trust corpus, and periodic stress-testing of our Company’s investment 
portfolio for credit and market risks in line with our investment policy.
Key Components of Our Restated Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss
Revenue from operations
Our revenue from operations comprises (i) revenue from contract with customers, and (ii) other operating revenues. 
Revenue from contract with customers:
• Transaction charges: represents fees we earn from trading activity across our stock exchange (including NSEIX). We 
generate transaction charges primarily from the cash market, futures and options. We also earn revenue from trading 
activity through the mutual funds platform, commodity derivatives, exchange-traded currency derivatives, wholesale 
404
debt market and interest rate futures. Transaction charges differ based on the type of product. 
• Listing services: comprise listing fees, book building fees and processing fees, which are fees charged to issuers for 
using our electronic bidding systems. Entities that list their securities on our Exchange (as well as NSEIX) pay one￾time initial listing fees, book building fees and processing fees at the time of listing. The initial listing fee is a 
fixed amount that is reviewed periodically, while book building and processing fees are determined based on the size
of a company’s proposed securities offering. In addition, entities pay a recurring annual listing fee at the beginning
of each year that their securities remain listed on our stock exchange in an amount determined based on total paid￾up share capital, bond or debenture capital as well as market capitalisation of companies. 
• Data Centre – Rack charges: are fees we receive from providing colocation data centre facilities to members of our 
Exchange and NSEIX. Rentals as well as incidental charges collected from members for providing racks are also 
classified under Data Centre - Rack charges.
• Data Connectivity charges: are the fees paid by market participants (such as brokers, institutional investors and high￾frequency traders) to our Exchange and NSEIX, to establish and maintain a physical or virtual link to connect and 
transact on the exchange’s trading system with charges determined based on subscription to different categories of 
Messages Per Second (MPS) per asset class. 
• Data Feed & Terminal services: include income generated from our data feed and terminal business, providing trading 
data (including real-time market data) sourced from our stock exchange through our online data feed service, data 
subscription packages, and data terminal services fees. We operate this business through our Subsidiaries, NSE Data 
& Analytics Limited and Cogencis Information Services Limited. 
• Licensing services: comprises fees for licensing our Nifty Indices for launching products linked to Nifty Indices to 
asset managers, to stock exchanges for introducing index linked derivatives contracts and other intermediaries such 
as brokers, investors, etc. that monitor the equity capital markets and derive revenue from usage of indices. 
We operate these indices through our Subsidiary, NSE Indices Limited.
• Clearing & Settlement Services: comprises revenue from Clearing & Settlement Services provided by our clearing 
corporation to market participants. We provide our Clearing & Settlement Services through our Subsidiaries, NCL and 
NSE IFSC Clearing Corporation Limited (“NSEICC”). 
• Others: primarily includes our remaining revenue streams that are not directly attributable to the services mentioned 
above, such as income from various ancillary services.
Other operating revenue: 
Other operating revenue primarily includes income from investments that is generated from sources of funds related to our 
operating activities. Income from investments primarily includes income that we derive from investing margin funds and cash 
collaterals received from clearing members as well as deposits received from trading members. We invest these funds primarily 
in government securities, corporate bonds, mutual funds and bank deposits. We follow our investments policy that is governed 
by prudential norms of investment and the SEBI guidelines (wherever applicable) in investing these funds and we earn interest 
income and income from redemption of units in mutual funds.

Contribution to Core Settlement Guarantee Fund
The Core SGF must be held in a separate account and serves as a financial safeguard to ensure timely settlement of trades in 
the event of clearing member defaults. SEBI guidelines prescribe how these funds may be used, and we cannot use the Core 
SGF for any purpose other than investment in safe, liquid instruments. The Core SGF is invested in government securities, 
fixed deposits and debt schemes of mutual funds (overnight and liquid schemes of the highest credit quality), with the income
from such investment added to corpus. As of June 30, 2026 and March 31, 2026, earmarked amounts pertaining to the Core 
SGF included ₹43,246.94 million and ₹51,876.84 million in non-current investments in quoted government securities at 
amortised cost, ₹13,118.26 million and ₹8,729.39 million in current investments in quoted government securities at amortised 
cost, ₹10,090.17 million and ₹9,914.02 million in current investments in unquoted mutual funds at FVTPL, accrued interest of 
₹46.37 million and ₹226.72 million shown under other financial assets (non-current) and ₹2,022.92 million and ₹1,975.97 
million shown under other financial assets (current), ₹2,900.10 million and ₹2,453.00 million in current accounts under bank 
balance other than cash and cash equivalents, ₹51,529.36 million and ₹47,327.29 million in fixed deposit with remaining 
maturity of less than 12 months and ₹10,886.99 million and ₹8,280.24 million in fixed deposit with remaining maturity of more 
than 12 months under other financial assets (non-current), respectively.
On March 23, 2023, our Board approved a voluntary contribution of 2% of transaction charges to the Core SGF. Following 
SEBI’s mandate requiring a minimum corpus of ₹105,000 million for equity derivatives products for clearing corporations 
with 40% or more clearing volume share, NCL achieved compliance by December 31, 2024. Consequently, on February 4, 
2025, our Board approved discontinuation of the voluntary contribution with effect from January 1, 2025. Accordingly, during 
Fiscal 2026, our Company contributed ₹5.76 million to the Core SGF, as against ₹2,340.89 million contributed in the preceding 
Fiscal 2025. During the three months period ended June 30, 2026, a further contribution of ₹50.00 million by NSE and ₹50.00 
million by NCL was made to the Core SGF towards new products added in electronic gold receipts. Additionally, ₹2,500.00 
million earmarked from General Reserves for the Commodity Derivatives SGF in Fiscal 2019 was de-allocated and reinstated 
during Fiscal 2024, pursuant to SEBI’s approval dated January 31, 2024. See “– Key Components of Our Restated Consolidated 
Statement of Profit and Loss – Contribution to Core Settlement Guarantee Fund” and “Restated Consolidated Financial 
Information – Notes to the Restated Consolidated Financial Information – Note 36 – Core Settlement Guarantee Fund” on 
pages 406 and 372, respectively.
Tax expenses
Our tax expense includes current tax and deferred tax. Provisions for current tax are made based on the estimated taxable
income for the current accounting period in accordance with the provisions of the Income Tax Act, 1961. Deferred tax results 
from temporary differences (related to timing) between the book and the taxable profits for the period and is accounted for
using the tax rates and laws that have been enacted or substantively enacted as of the balance sheet date.

Income

million in the three months period ended June 30, 2025. This increase was driven by increase in transaction charges on account 
of growth in volume primarily in cash market and equity options, higher income on investments, data feed & terminal services,
and clearing & settlement services partly offset by lower other non-operating income.
Revenue from operations
• Revenue from contracts with customers

months period ended June 30, 2026 from ₹31,536.00 million in the three months period ended June 30, 2025. The 
increase in transaction charges is on account of growth in volume in cash market products as ADTV increased to 
₹1,359,487.29 million in the three months period ended June 30, 2026 from ₹1,085,421.75 million in the three months 
period ended June 30, 2025, equity options products (premium value) with ADTV increasing to ₹643,517.81 million 
in the three months period ended June 30, 2026 from ₹555,136.09 million in the three months period ended June 30, 
2025, partially offset by lower volume of equity futures as ADTV decreased to ₹1,530,788.97 million in the three 
months period ended June 30, 2026 from ₹1,684,296.36 million in the three months period ended June 30, 2025. This 
was also supported by higher price realisation for cash market, equity futures and equity options. Our revenue from 
transaction charges accounted for 79.44% of our revenue from operations in the three months period ended June 30, 
2026 compared to 78.20% in the three months period ended June 30, 2025.

as the Core SGF has reached the desired corpus of ₹105,000 million for equity derivatives products as advised by SEBI in its 
letter dated May 3, 2024. For details on Core SGF see “ – Significant Factors Affecting Our Financial Condition and Results 
of Operations – Regulatory Oversight and Governmental Policies” on page 400.
Exceptional items 
Our profit on the sale of investment in associates, reported as exceptional items was ₹12,094.72 million during Fiscal 2025, 
arising from the sale of its entire stake of 20.34% in Protean eGov Technologies Limited resulting in a profit of ₹11,549.28 
million and sale of part stake of 4.21% in Power Exchange India Limited resulting in a profit of ₹545.44 million. In comparison, 
profit on the sale of investment in associates of ₹814.35 million arising from the sale of 4.71% stake in Protean eGov 
Technologies Limited was reported as an exceptional item in Fiscal 2024. 
Tax expenses
Our total tax expenses increased by 39.28% to ₹38,690.30 million in Fiscal 2025 from ₹27,778.00 million in Fiscal 2024. This 
was primarily due to an increase in our current tax on account of the increase in our profit before tax from Continuing 
Operations. This was partially offset by reduction in deferred tax expenses primarily due to a decrease in deferred tax liability 
on mark-to-market investments resulting from the reduction in the long-term capital gains tax rate from 20.00% to 12.50%.
Profit for the year from Continuing Operations
For the foregoing reasons, our profit for the year from Continuing Operations increased by 38.06% to ₹116,057.48 million in 
Fiscal 2025 from ₹84,064.80 million in Fiscal 2024.
Key Balance Sheet Items
Trade Receivables
Trade receivables as of June 30, 2026 decreased by 8.88% to ₹22,491.37 million from ₹24,682.13 million as of March 31, 
2026, primarily due to lower trading volumes in June 2026 compared to March 2026. Trade receivables as of March 31, 2026 
increased by 63.22% to ₹24,682.13 million from ₹15,122.24 million as of March 31, 2025. This increase was primarily driven 
by a 67.50% increase in unbilled amounts, attributable to significantly higher trading volumes in March 2026 compared to 
March 2025. Trade receivables as of March 31, 2025 decreased by 18.90% to ₹15,122.24 million from ₹18,646.60 million as 
of March 31, 2024. This decrease was primarily attributable to lower unbilled amounts because of reduced trading volumes in 
March 2025.
Right of Use Assets
Right of use assets primarily comprise leases for land, buildings and plant and equipment.
Right of use assets increased by 436.06% from ₹4,211.33 million as of March 31, 2026 to ₹22,575.09 million as of June 30, 
2026, primarily due to land taken on lease from Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (“MMRDA”) and 
renewal of existing lease for office premises, which was partially offset by depreciation charge on right of use assets during the 
three months period ended June 30, 2026. Right of use assets decreased by 20.67% from ₹5,308.40 million as of March 31, 
2025 to ₹4,211.33 million as of March 31, 2026, primarily due to depreciation charge on right of use assets during Fiscal 2026, 
which was partially offset by the addition of new lease premises by NSE and NSE Clearing during Fiscal 2026. Further, right 
of use assets increased by 215.11% from ₹1,684.64 million as of March 31, 2024 to ₹5,308.40 million as of March 31, 2025, 
primarily due to the addition of new lease premises by NSE amounting to ₹4,294.72 million during Fiscal 2025.

Our Segments
We have three reporting segments (i) Trading Services, (ii) Clearing Services, and (iii) Others. 
(i) Trading Services: We offer services relating to trading in the equity, equity derivatives, debt, exchange-traded 
currency derivatives and commodity derivatives segments. Revenue from the trading services segment primarily 
includes transaction charges, revenue from listing services, revenue from Data Centre - Rack charges and revenue 
from Data Connectivity charges, among others.
(ii) Clearing Services: We offer clearing and settlement of trades executed in the cash markets, futures and options, 
currency derivatives and commodity derivatives segments, and associated investment income.
(iii) Others: comprises the results of operations from data feed services, data terminal services, strategic investments and 
licensing services.

Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures 
Financial Risk Management
Our business activities expose us to a variety of financial risks, namely liquidity risk, market risks and credit risk. Our risk 
management policies are established to identify and analyse the risks faced by us, to set appropriate risk limits and controls and 
to monitor risks and adherence to limits. Risk management policies and systems are reviewed regularly to reflect changes in 
market conditions and our activities. Our senior management has the overall responsibility for developing and implementing 
our risk management policies. We have constituted a Risk Management Committee to oversee the implementation of our risk 
management policies. Our Risk Management Committee is supported by the Treasury Committee that provides assurance that 
our financial risk activities are governed by appropriate policies and procedures and that financial risks are identified, measured 
and managed in accordance with our policies and risk objectives. We have a dedicated Treasury department to ensure 
investments are made as per the approved prudential norms of investment.
Management of liquidity risk
Liquidity risk is the risk that we will face difficulties in meeting our obligations associated with our financial liabilities. Our 
approach to managing liquidity is to ensure that we will have sufficient funds to meet our liabilities when due without incurring 
avoidable costs. In doing this, management considers both normal and stressed conditions. A material and sustained shortfall 
in our cash flow could impair investor confidence.
We maintain a cautious funding strategy, with a positive cash balance throughout the three months period ended June 30, 2026 
and June 30, 2025, and the years ended March 31, 2026; March 31, 2025 and March 31, 2024. Cash flows from operating and 
investing activities provides the funds to service the financing of liabilities on a day-to-day basis.
Our treasury department regularly monitors the rolling forecasts to ensure we have sufficient cash on an on-going basis to meet 
operational needs. Any short term surplus cash generated by the operations, over and above the amount required for working 
capital management and other operational requirements, is retained as cash and cash equivalents (to the extent required) and 
any excess is invested in interest bearing deposits and other marketable debt investments not invested in equity linked funds
including the government securities, mutual funds and exchange-traded funds with appropriate maturities to optimise the cash 
returns on investments while ensuring sufficient liquidity to meet our liabilities.
Management of market risk
Our size and operations result in us being exposed to the following market risks that arise from our use of financial instruments:
• price risk; and
• interest rate risk.
The above risks may affect our income and expenses, or the value of our financial instruments. The objective of our 
management of market risk is to maintain this risk within acceptable parameters, while optimising returns.
Management of foreign exchange risk
We enter transactions requiring remittance in foreign currency at a future date. We use forward contracts to manage our 
exposure to currency fluctuations on foreign exchange settlements arising from anticipated payment remittance transactions. 
Forward contracts are governed by the forex risk management policy as approved by the Board of National Stock Exchange of 
India Limited and are used as part of our risk management strategy to mitigate the impact of exchange rate volatility. We follow 
the Mark-to-Market (MTM) method for accounting of these foreign exchange forward contracts and measure the open contracts 
at each reporting date at fair value. Any gains or losses arising from changes in fair value and cancellation/rollover of the
forward contracts are recognised in the Restated Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss.
Management of credit risk
Credit risk is the risk of financial loss if a customer or counterparty fails to meet its contractual obligations.
Trade receivables
Concentrations of credit risk with respect to trade receivables are limited, due to our customer base being large and diverse and 
also on account of members’ deposits kept by us as collateral which can be utilised in case of member default. All trade 
receivables are reviewed and assessed for default on a quarterly basis. Based on historical experience of collecting receivables, 
supported by the level of default, our assessment of credit risk is low. Accordingly, provision for expected credit loss on trade 
receivables is not material as they are settled fairly quickly.
Other financial assets
We maintain exposure in cash and cash equivalents, term deposits with banks / financial institutions and investments in 
marketable debt investments including the government securities, mutual funds and exchange-traded funds. We have a 
431
diversified portfolio of investments with various number of counter parties which have secure credit ratings; hence the risk is 
reduced. Individual risk limits are set for each counter party based on financial position, credit rating and past experience. 
Credit limits and concentration of exposures are actively monitored by our Treasury department. Our investments are primarily 
into AAA / AA high rating instruments and based on the historical experience of investee company, our assessment for credit 
risk is low. Accordingly, the provision for expected credit loss on other financial assets is not material.
Capital management
We consider the following components of our restated consolidated statement of assets and liabilities to be managed capital:
Total equity (as shown in the restated consolidated statement of assets and liabilities, including equity share capital, securities 
premium reserve, includes retained earnings and profits, other reserves).
We aim to manage our capital so as to safeguard our ability to continue as a going concern and to optimise returns to our 
shareholders. Our capital structure is based on management’s judgement of the appropriate balance of key elements in order to
meet our strategic and day-to-day needs. We consider the amount of capital in proportion to risk and manage the capital 
structure in light of changes in economic conditions and the risk characteristics of the underlying assets. This has been 
determined taking into consideration various factors and risks including market risk, credit risk, members default risk, 
operational risk, etc. In order to maintain or adjust the capital structure, we may adjust the amount of dividends paid to 
shareholders, return capital to shareholders or issue new shares.
Our policy is to maintain a stable and strong capital structure with a focus on total equity so as to maintain investor, creditor 
and market confidence and to sustain future development and growth of our business. We will take appropriate steps in order 
to maintain, or if necessary, adjust, our capital structure. We are not subject to financial covenants in any of our significant
financing agreements.
Our management monitors the return on capital as well as the level of dividends to shareholders. Our goal is to continue to be 
able to return excess liquidity to shareholders by continuing to distribute dividends in future periods.

Material accounting policies 
Revenue recognition
We recognise the revenue in accordance with Ind AS 115 - Revenue from Contracts with customers. We derive revenue 
primarily from transaction charges, listing fee, book building fee, processing fee, Data Centre - Rack charges, Data Connectivity 
charges, online data feed and terminal charges, index licensing and data subscription fee, Clearing & Settlement Services, etc. 
Revenue is recognised upon transfer of control to the customers by rendering of contractual services and on completion of all
the performance obligations under the contract with a reasonable certainty of the ultimate realisation of the dues. Revenue is 
recognised in an amount that reflects the consideration which we expect to receive in exchange for the services rendered. We 
recognise revenue in the period in which we satisfy our performance obligation by transferring promised goods or services to 
the customer. The major sources of revenue and our accounting policy are as follows:
(i) Transaction charges – revenue in respect of trading transactions on Exchange is recognised in accordance with our fee 
scales at a point in time as and when the transaction is completed.
(ii) Listing fees - Revenue for listing fees is recognised when the listing event has taken place, annual listing fees and 
processing fees in relation to listing are recognised on a straight-line basis over the period to which they relate.
(iii) Book building fees – revenue is recognised at a point in time on completion of the book building process.
(iv) Data Centre – Rack charges - revenue is recognised over the period of the contract with the customer. The revenue is 
calculated based on the specified charges for data centre racks and is recognised in the period in which the performance 
obligation is satisfied.
(v) Data Connectivity charges - revenue is recognised over the period of the contract with the customer. Connectivity charges 
are the fees paid by the trading members of the Company to establish and maintain a physical or virtual link to the 
exchange’s trading system.
(vi) Clearing & Settlement Services - revenue in respect of clearing and settlement of transactions executed on Exchange is 
recognised in accordance with the fee scales at a point in time as and when the transaction is completed.
(vii) Revenue from Technology services comprises Application Development and Maintenance services, E-learning Solutions, 
Online examination services, Infrastructure Management Services, IT security services and IT cloud services. Revenue 
from time and material and job contracts is recognised using the output method measured by units delivered, efforts 
expended, number of transactions processed, etc. Revenue related to fixed price maintenance and support services 
contracts, where we are standing ready to provide services is recognised based on time elapsed on a straight-line basis over 
the period of performance. In respect of other fixed-price contracts, revenue is recognised over a period of time using 
percentage-of-completion method of accounting with contract costs incurred determining the degree of completion of the 
performance obligation. The contract costs used in computing the revenues include cost of fulfilling warranty obligations. 
Revenue from online examination services is recognised on the basis of exams conducted and where there are multiple 
performance obligations, revenue is recognised using percentage-of-completion method of accounting with contract costs 
incurred determining the degree of completion of the performance obligation. Revenue from the sale of distinct third-party 
hardware is recognised at the point in time when control is transferred to the customer. The solutions offered by us may 
include supply of third-party equipment or software. In such cases, revenue for supply of such third-party equipment or 
software is recorded on a gross or net basis depending on whether we are acting as the principal or as an agent. We 
recognise revenue at the gross amount of consideration when we are acting as a principal and at net amount of consideration 
when we are acting as an agent.
(viii) Subscription and other fees related to data feed & terminal services and licensing services – revenue is recognised 
over a period of time to which the fee relates.
(ix) Other services – all other revenue is recognised in the period in which the performance obligation is satisfied over a period 
of time or point in time.
(x) Financing Component – We do not have any contracts where the period between the transfer of the promised services to 
the customer and payment by the customer exceeds one year. As a consequence, we do not adjust any of the transaction 
prices for the time value of money. 
We consider the terms of the contract in determining the transaction price. The transaction price is based upon the amount we 
expect to be entitled to in exchange for transferring of promised services to the customer after deducting allowances and 
incentives such as discounts, volume rebates etc. Revenue excludes any taxes and duties collected on behalf of the government. 
433
In respect of members who have been declared as defaulters by us, all amounts (dues) remaining to be recovered from such 
defaulters, net of available security and insurance cover available if any, till the date of being declared as defaulters are written 
off as bad debts. All subsequent recoveries are accounted when received. In respect of Listed companies and other trade 
receivables where no such deposit is available with the exchange, as per the current practice, the amounts which are outstanding 
for more than 2 years are subject to 100% impairment. For amounts lying uncollected beyond a period of 3 years are written 
off. All subsequent recoveries are accounted when received.
Business Combinations
The acquisition method of accounting is used to account for all business combinations, regardless of whether equity instruments
or other assets are acquired. The consideration transferred for the acquisition of a subsidiary comprises:
• the fair values of the assets transferred;
• liabilities incurred to the former owners of the acquired business;
• equity interests issued by us; and
• fair value of any asset or liability resulting from a contingent consideration arrangement.
Identifiable assets acquired and liabilities and contingent liabilities assumed in a business combination are, with limited 
exceptions, measured initially at their fair values at the acquisition date. We recognise any non-controlling interest in the 
acquired entity on an acquisition-by-acquisition basis either at fair value or at the non-controlling interest’s proportionate share 
of the acquired entity’s net identifiable assets.
Acquisition-related costs are expensed as incurred. The excess of the purchase consideration, as given below, over the fair 
value of the net identifiable assets acquired as of the date of acquisition, is recorded as goodwill;
• consideration transferred;
• amount of any non-controlling interest in the acquired entity, and
• acquisition-date fair value of any previous equity interest in the acquired entity.
If the purchase consideration is less than the fair value of the net identifiable assets of the business acquired, the difference is 
recognised in other comprehensive income and accumulated in equity as capital reserve provided, there is clear evidence of the 
underlying reasons for classifying the business combination as a bargain purchase. In other cases, the bargain purchase gain is 
recognised directly in equity as capital reserve. Where settlement of any part of cash consideration is deferred, the amounts 
payable in the future are discounted to their present value as of the date of exchange. The discount rate used is the entity’s
incremental borrowing rate, being the rate at which a similar borrowing could be obtained from an independent financier under 
comparable terms and conditions. Contingent consideration is classified either as equity or a financial liability. Amounts 
classified as a financial liability are subsequently remeasured to fair value with changes in fair value recognised in profit or 
loss. If the business consideration is achieved in stages, the acquisition date carrying value of the acquirer’s previously held 
equity interest in the acquiree is remeasured to fair value at the acquisition date. Any gains or losses arising from such 
remeasurement are recognised in profit or loss or other comprehensive income, as appropriate.
Leases
Our lease asset classes primarily consist of leases for land, buildings and equipment. We assess whether a contract contains a 
lease, at inception of the contract. Ind AS 116 defines a lease as a contract, or a part of a contract, that conveys the right to use 
an asset (the underlying asset) for a period of time in exchange for consideration. To assess whether a contract conveys the 
right to control the use of an identified asset, we assess whether: (i) the contract involves the use of an identified asset (ii) we 
have substantially all of the economic benefits from use of the asset through the period of the lease and (iii) we have the right 
to direct the use of the asset. At the date of commencement of the lease, we recognise a right-of-use asset and a corresponding 
lease liability for all lease arrangements in which we are a lessee, except for leases with a term of twelve months or less (short 
term leases) and low value leases. For these short-term and low value leases, we recognise the lease payments as an operating 
expense on a straight-line basis over the term of the lease. The lease payments are discounted using the interest rate implicit in 
the lease. If the rate cannot be readily determined, which is generally the case for our leases, the lessee’s incremental borrowing 
rate is used, being the rate that the individual lessee would have to pay to borrow the funds necessary to obtain an asset of
similar value to the right-of-use asset in a similar economic environment with similar terms, security and conditions.
To determine the incremental borrowing rate, we:
• where possible, use recent third-party financing received by the individual lessee as a starting point, adjusted to reflect 
changes in financing conditions since third-party financing was received.
• use a build-up approach that starts with a risk-free interest rate adjusted for credit risk for leases held by the Group, 
which does not have recent third-party financing.
434
• make adjustments specific to the lease.
If a readily observable amortising loan rate is available to the individual lessee (through recent financing or market data) which 
has a similar payment profile to the lease, we use that rate as a starting point to determine the incremental borrowing rate. The 
lease liability is initially measured at amortised cost at the present value of the future lease payments. The lease payments are 
discounted using the interest rate implicit in the lease or, if not readily determinable, using the incremental borrowing rates. 
Right-of-use assets are generally depreciated over the shorter of the asset’s useful life and the lease term on a straight-line basis. 
If we are reasonably certain to exercise a purchase option, the right-of-use asset is depreciated over the underlying asset’s useful 
life. Refer note 1(ii)(f) for the other accounting policies relevant to leases.
Trade receivables
Trade receivables are amounts due from customers for services performed in the ordinary course of business and reflect our 
unconditional right to consideration (that is, payment is due only on the passage of time). Trade receivables are recognised 
initially based on the transaction price as they do not contain significant financing components. We hold the trade receivables 
with the objective of collecting the contractual cash flows and therefore measure them subsequently at amortised cost using the 
effective interest method, less loss allowance for credit impairment.
Financial assets
• Classification of financial assets at amortised cost: We classify our financial assets at amortised cost only if both of 
the following criteria are met:
o Asset is held with a business model whose objective is to collect the contractual cash flows.
o The contractual terms give rise to cash flows that are solely payments of principal and interest.
Financial assets classified at amortised cost comprise trade receivables, bonds, debentures and government securities.
• Classification of financial assets at fair value through other comprehensive income (FVOCI): Financial assets at 
FVOCI comprise:
o Equity securities (listed or unlisted) which are not held for trading, and for which we have irrevocably elected 
at initial recognition to recognise changes in fair value through OCI rather than profit or loss. These are 
strategic investments and we consider this classification to be more relevant.
o Debt securities where the contractual cash flows are solely principal, and interest and the objective of our 
business model is achieved both by collecting contractual cash flows and selling financial assets.
• Classification of financial assets at fair value through profit or loss (FVTPL): We classify the following financial 
assets at FVTPL:
o Debt investments (Mutual funds) that do not qualify for measurement at either amortised cost or FVOCI.
o Equity instruments for which the entity has not elected to recognise fair value gains and losses through OCI.
Property, plant and equipment (including Capital Work in Progress)
Freehold land is carried at the historical cost of acquisition. All other items of property, plant and equipment are stated at 
historical cost less depreciation. Cost comprises purchase price and any initial directly attributable cost of bringing the asset to 
its working condition for its intended use.
Depreciation methods, estimated useful lives and residual value
Depreciation is calculated using the straight-line method to allocate their cost, net of their residual values, over their estimated 
useful lives as prescribed in Schedule II of the Companies Act, 2013 except in respect of certain categories of assets, where the 
useful life of the assets has been assessed based on the management’s technical evaluation. The estimated useful lives are as 
mentioned below:
Block of Asset Useful life
Building 60 years
Furniture and fixture 5 to 10 years
Office equipment 4 to 5 years
Electrical equipment & installations 10 years
Computer systems - office automation and others 3 to 4 years
Telecommunication systems 4 years
Trading systems 4 years
Clearing & Settlement Systems 4 years
Motor Vehicle 4 years
435
The useful lives for computer systems office automation, computer systems – others, telecommunication systems, trading 
systems and clearing & settlement systems have been determined based on technical evaluation done by the management’s 
expert which are lower than those specified by Schedule II to the Companies Act, 2013, in order to reflect the actual usage of 
the assets. We believe that the technically evaluated useful lives, different from Schedule II of the Companies Act, 2013, best 
represent the period over which these assets are expected to be used. The residual values are not more than 5% of the original 
cost of the asset. The assets’ residual values and useful lives are reviewed at the end of each reporting period and adjusted on 
a prospective basis if appropriate.
Investment properties
Property that is held for long-term rental yields or for capital appreciation or both, and that is not occupied by us, is accounted 
as investment property. Investment property is measured initially at its cost, including related transaction costs. Investment 
properties are depreciated using the straight-line method over their estimated useful lives. Investment properties generally have 
an estimated useful life of 60 years. The useful life has been determined based on technical evaluation performed by the 
management expert.
Intangible assets
Intangible assets purchased are measured at cost as of the date of acquisition, as applicable, less accumulated amortisation and 
accumulated impairment, if any.
(i) Goodwill: Goodwill represents the excess of purchase consideration over the fair value of the net identifiable assets
acquired as of the date of acquisition. Goodwill on acquisitions of business and subsidiaries is included in intangible assets. 
Goodwill is not amortised, but it is tested for impairment annually, or more frequently if events or changes in circumstances
indicate that it might be impaired and is carried at cost less accumulated impairment losses. Gains and losses on the disposal 
of an entity include the carrying amount of goodwill relating to the entity sold. Goodwill is allocated to cash-generating 
units for the purpose of impairment testing. The allocation is made to those cash-generating units or groups of cash￾generating units that are expected to benefit from the business combination in which the goodwill arose. The units or 
groups of units are identified at the lowest level at which goodwill is monitored for internal management purposes, which 
in our case are the operating segments.
(ii) Otherintangible assets: Costs associated with maintaining software programmes are recognised as an expense as incurred. 
Development costs of internally generated intangible assets that are directly attributable to the design and testing of 
identifiable and unique software products controlled by us are recognised as intangible assets when the following criteria 
are met:
• it is technically feasible to complete the software so that it will be available for use;
• management intends to complete the software and use or sell it;
• there is an ability to use or sell the software;
• it can be demonstrated how the software will generate probable future economic benefits;
• adequate technical, financial and other resources to complete the development and to use or sell the software are 
available; and
• the expenditure attributable to the software during its development can be reliably measured.
Directly attributable costs that are capitalised as part of the software include employee costs and an appropriate portion of 
relevant overheads. Research expenditure and development expenditure that do not meet the criteria in (ii) above are 
recognised as an expense as incurred. Development costs previously recognised as an expense are not recognised as an
asset in a subsequent period. Capitalised development costs are recorded as intangible assets and amortised from the point 
at which the asset is available for use. Computer software is amortised over a period of 4 years.
Core Settlement Guarantee Fund
We contribute to Settlement Guarantee Fund/ Core Settlement Guarantee Fund in accordance with Securities and Exchange 
Board of India (Stock Exchanges and Clearing Corporations) Regulations, 2018. The National Stock Exchange of India Limited 
(the Parent company) contributes amounts pertaining to Minimum Required Corpus to the Core Settlement Guarantee Fund, 
which is determined as per SEBI guidelines. The contribution to Settlement Guarantee Fund/ Core Settlement Guarantee Fund 
by the Parent Company is recorded as an expense in the Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss and contribution by its 
clearing corporation subsidiary is recorded as an appropriation from our retained earnings and such amounts are separately 
disclosed as Core Settlement Guarantee Fund in the Consolidated balance sheet. Trades executed on the Exchange platform 
are cleared and settled by the clearing corporations under interoperability framework prescribed by SEBI. Post interoperability, 
the stock exchange is required to proportionately contribute to Core SGF of the clearing corporations, namely NSE Clearing 
Limited (NCL), BSE Clearing Limited (BSECL) and Metropolitan Clearing Corporation of India Limited (MCCIL) which 
clears and settles the trades of the stock exchange. Such contributions are also recorded as an expense and separately disclosed 
436
in the balance sheet. As per SEBI guidelines, we invest balances in Core Settlement Guarantee Fund in prescribed category of 
securities which are earmarked/restricted and income earned on such investments are attributed directly and credited to the 
fund balance. Fines and penalties recovered by us from members are also directly attributed and credited to the fund balance.
We record a loss in its Statement of Profit and Loss in case of a default event, as per the default waterfall defined under the 
SEBI regulations, including by utilisation of the Core Settlement Guarantee Fund balance.

OUTSTANDING LITIGATION AND MATERIAL DEVELOPMENTS
Except as disclosed in this section, there are no outstanding (i) criminal proceedings (including matters which are at FIR stage even

Information i.e., Fiscal 2026, being ₹ 6,373.94 million; or
(c) 5% of the average of absolute value of profit or loss after tax, for the last three financial years as per the Restated 
Consolidated Financial Information, i.e., Fiscals 2024, 2025 and 2026 being ₹ 5,132.58 million.
in this case being ₹ 3,320.26 million (“Materiality Threshold”).

the Materiality Threshold, even though the value or expected impact in terms of value involved in an individual litigation may

C. All outstanding litigation which may not meet the Materiality Threshold or is not quantifiable, but where an adverse outcome 
would materially and adversely affect the business, prospects, operations, performance, financial position or reputation of our

members of the Senior Management from third parties (excluding notices issued by statutory or regulatory or taxation authorities or

National Securities Clearing Corporation Limited (now NSE Clearing Limited) filed a criminal application dated May
